title: Ampleness reflected by the abelian quotient of a semiabelian variety
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $C/k$ an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and $T/k$ a torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Let $G/k$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type group scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sc-group-scheme], and suppose that $1\to T\to G\xrightarrow{q}C\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site], with $q$ a $T$-torsor: it is faithfully flat of finite presentation and $G\times_kT\to G\times_CG$, $(g,t)\mapsto(g,gt)$, is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any invertible module $D$ on $C$ [def-sc-invertible-module], if its tensor pullback $q^*D$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample on $G$, then $D$ is ample on $C$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No splitting of $T$, perfection of $k$, or symmetry of $D$ is required.

source.place: XI 1.11, field case; compare Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, Proposition 3.3.3.6 proof and Lemma 4.2.1.8 proof, which explicitly use this implication. Raynaud original WANTED.

proof.text: Let $F=\bar k$. The base change $C_F$ is abelian. The base changes of $G$ are smooth, separated and finite type, and $T_F$ is split by the definition of a torus. Base change the fppf cover $q$; it remains an fppf cover and of finite presentation. The torsor isomorphism remains an isomorphism because its inverse also base changes, and the group identities remain identities under fibre product. Thus the same hypotheses hold over $F$, with split torus. Relative ample base change applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $q_F^*D_F$ ample. It suffices to prove $D_F$ ample: $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a singleton fpqc cover (a nonzero vector space extension is faithfully flat), so relative ample fpqc descent gives $D$ ample. In the following steps work over $F$ and omit the subscripts.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, lemma-descending-property-ample; base change Tag 0893 in morphisms.tex. Field reduction as in Milne AV I Proposition 6.6(c).

proof.text: Choose an ample invertible module $H$ on $C$ using projectivity of abelian varieties. The module $q^*(H^\vee)$ is invertible, hence finite type and quasi-coherent. Apply ample coherent twisting on $G$ to this module and the ample module $q^*D$. For some $n\geq1$, the module $q^*(H^\vee)\otimes(q^*D)^{\otimes n}\simeq q^*(H^\vee\otimes D^{\otimes n})$ is generated by finitely many global sections. Evaluate at the identity of $G$: its fibre is a nonzero one-dimensional $F$-vector space, so at least one of the generating sections is nonzero. Put $L=D^{\otimes n}\otimes H^\vee$. We have $\Gamma(G,q^*L)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, ample implies eventual global generation; Milne AV I Theorem 6.4 supplies H.

proof.text: Apply the split-torus section-extraction lemma to $q:G\to C$ and $L$. Its base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because the abelian variety is proper. We obtain an invertible module $N$ on $C$ with $q^*N\simeq\mathcal O_G$ and a nonzero section of $R=L\otimes N$. The semiabelian Picard-pullback-kernel lemma applies to this same exact split-torus group extension over the algebraically closed field $F$ and says that $N$ is algebraically trivial on $C$.

source.place: Tags 0EKK and 0EKL, the section-extraction input; Milne AV I Proposition 9.3 is the existing Picard-kernel input.

proof.text: Apply effective-square generation to $J=C$ and the nonzero section of $R$: an abelian variety is commutative, and it has semiabelian geometric fibres with torus rank zero: for every algebraically closed field $K$ and morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ the base change $C_K$ is an abelian variety over $K$ by the field-extension lemma, and the identity $C_K\to C_K$ with the trivial split torus of rank zero as kernel is the required exact sequence. Smoothness gives local finite presentation; finite type gives quasi-compactness and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness, so $C/F$ is of finite presentation. Hence $R^{\otimes2}$ is generated by global sections.

source.place: I Corollary 5.3 and theorem of the square, translation argument packaged by the existing effective-square-generation node.

proof.text: The module $H^{\otimes2}$ is ample. For any $x\in C$, choose $a\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(C,H^{\otimes2a})$ with $x\in C_s$ affine, and choose $t\in\Gamma(C,R^{\otimes2})$ nonzero at $x$. The section $s\otimes t^{\otimes a}$ of $(H^{\otimes2}\otimes R^{\otimes2})^{\otimes a}$ has nonvanishing locus $C_s\cap C_t$: over every residue field a tensor product of nonzero vectors in one-dimensional spaces is nonzero, and it vanishes if either factor vanishes. This intersection is affine by the affine-cap-section-open lemma. Since $C$ is quasi-compact, the definition of ampleness shows $H^{\otimes2}\otimes R^{\otimes2}$ ample. Cancelling $H^{\otimes2}$ against $(H^\vee)^{\otimes2}$ identifies this module with $D^{\otimes2n}\otimes N^{\otimes2}$. This is precisely the elementary proof of Stacks 0890 in this case, rather than an appeal to a node which only states ample tensor ample.

source.place: Tag 0890, lemma-ample-tensor-globally-generated, explicit proof; Tag 01PV, lemma-affine-cap-s-open.

proof.text: Algebraically trivial invertible modules form a group under tensor product, so $N^{\otimes2}$ is algebraically trivial. Apply clause (ii) of algebraic-equivalence-norm to $C$, which is commutative, proper hence separated, smooth and of finite type, and semiabelian with $r=0$ and $A=C$ over the algebraically closed field $F$, with $P=D^{\otimes2n}$ and $T=N^{\otimes2}$: the ampleness just proved implies $D^{\otimes2n}$ ample. By the ample definition this implies $D$ ample, since a section of $(D^{\otimes2n})^{\otimes b}$ is a section of $D^{\otimes2nb}$ with the same affine nonvanishing locus, and $2nb>0$ for $b>0$. This proves the assertion over $F$; the fpqc descent in step 1 concludes over the original field. No symmetry of $D$ has been used.

source.place: I Proposition 6.6(c) and Picard-zero ampleness invariance, the latter packaged by the existing algebraic-equivalence-norm node. Assembly written by Q83.

proof_origin.place: I Theorem 6.4, Proposition 6.6(c), theorem of the square, and Proposition 9.3; assembly using Stacks 01Q3, 0890, 0EKK, 0EKL, 0D3C. Raynaud XI 1.11 original unavailable.
